quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: There are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked vehicles to your right. Where should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles.
In the middle between both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the middle between both sides.
questions.explanation: Steer in the middle, between the oncoming cars and the parked cars. This is the safest path.

questions.question: Roads are slippery after rain starts. What should you do when the road is slippery?

options.text: Avoid turning and stopping at high speeds.
Test your tire grip while going uphill.
Look less far ahead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid turning and stopping at high speeds.
questions.explanation: Wet roads make tires slip easily. Drive slowly and avoid sharp turns or hard stops to prevent skidding.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in a construction zone?

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Be ready for anything unexpected.
Expect construction workers to get out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for anything unexpected.
questions.explanation: Construction zones can have sudden surprises. Drive carefully to keep yourself, other drivers, and workers safe.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in construction zones?

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers warn you about work zones. Be extra careful when you see them.

questions.question: What happens if you brake hard on ice and snow?

options.text: You stop faster.
Your front wheels lock up and you lose steering.
Your brakes won't freeze.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your front wheels lock up and you lose steering.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on ice or snow can lock your front wheels, so you cannot steer. Slow down before you need to brake hard.

questions.question: What should you do when backing up?

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Only use your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Mirrors don't show everything behind your car. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, start from which lane?

options.text: Any lane (if it is safe).
The leftmost lane.
The center lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The leftmost lane.
questions.explanation: Start your left turn from the leftmost lane of the road.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use low beam headlights.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, use low beams and slow down. If you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the lane next to the solid line.
No one can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane next to the broken line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane next to the broken line.
questions.explanation: The broken line means you can pass. The solid line means the other direction cannot pass.

questions.question: Motorcycles and scooters are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down.
Keep looking around constantly.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep looking around constantly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss. Always watch for them, especially in blind spots.

questions.question: How do you prevent hydroplaning in wet weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slowing down prevents it.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use turn signals?

options.text: Only when leaving the curb.
Only when pulling next to the curb.
When pulling next to or leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling next to or leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: Signal both when you approach the curb and when you leave it.

questions.question: How do you avoid carbon monoxide poisoning?

options.text: Have your exhaust system checked for leaks.
Keep your engine off in a closed garage.
Do both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide is odorless and dangerous. Check your exhaust system and never run your engine in a closed garage.

questions.question: You have a green light but traffic blocks the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter to claim your right-of-way.
Don't enter until you can get all the way across.
Drive in and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't enter until you can get all the way across.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, only enter the intersection if you can completely cross before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Stop sign ahead.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. Slow down because it takes longer to stop on wet pavement.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
There is two-way traffic.
You are approaching a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic moves in both directions on this road.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your freeway lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room if you safely can.
Speed up to keep your spot.
Don't change your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room if you safely can.
questions.explanation: Help merging traffic by making room in your lane when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Can you drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, if the vehicle ahead is turning left.
Yes, if there are two or more lanes in your direction.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never drive off the road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When can you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle ahead moves right to let you pass.
When the yellow line on your side is broken.
When the yellow line on the other side is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the yellow line on your side is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: How does vehicle speed affect stopping distance and crash severity?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line between traffic lanes mean?

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. You cannot pass other vehicles in either direction.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in work zones?

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.
Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: In work zones, stay away from barriers, trucks, equipment, and workers. Keep extra distance between your vehicle and others. Do not tailgate.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle to your right.
When you can see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You need enough space between you and the other vehicle before returning to your lane. You can return to your lane when you see both headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Keeping one car length between you and the car ahead.
Looking only at the car in front of you.
Constantly scanning ahead for possible hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Constantly scanning ahead for possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead and around for potential dangers. Do not stare only at the road directly in front of you. Watch for vehicles around you while scanning ahead.

questions.question: What must you do when a school bus stops to load or unload children?

options.text: Stop completely until all children leave the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in.
Change lanes and pass the bus slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in.
questions.explanation: Stop when you see a school bus with flashing red lights and a stop arm extended. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in before moving. Also check that no children are crossing the road.

questions.question: You are in the center lane of an expressway and cars are passing you on both sides. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: Use the right lanes on expressways and interstates unless you are passing or turning left. If you are driving slower than the traffic flow, use the right lane.

questions.question: Is it legal to drive if medication impairs your driving?

options.text: No, never.
Yes, if you do not feel drowsy.
Yes, if a doctor prescribed it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: You cannot drive under the influence of any substance that affects your driving. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: What must you do on a green arrow?

options.text: Yield to vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only.
Wait four seconds before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means go. Turn in the direction the arrow points. But first, yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: An oncoming car has high beams on at night, blinding you. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane. Watch the other vehicle from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane with oncoming traffic ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your wheels left to prepare for the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Signal about 100 feet before your turn. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This prevents another vehicle from pushing you into oncoming traffic if it hits you from behind.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Wait for a green light.
Slow down and cross carefully.
Stop before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be aware. Proceed with caution. Watch for crossing traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: You are exiting the freeway on a curved downhill ramp. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down before the curve.
Slow to the freeway speed limit.
Start braking after you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You may not see hazards ahead. Braking in a curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles.
Wherever signs and pavement markings permit passing.
In a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever signs and pavement markings permit passing.
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, parking lots, or alleyways. Never pass on curves or hills where you cannot see ahead. Assume an oncoming vehicle is just out of sight. Only pass where signs and markings allow it and only if you have enough space.

questions.question: Must you give your name and vehicle information after a collision?

options.text: Only if someone is injured.
Only if damage is over $500.
Yes, every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, every time.
questions.explanation: You must stop at every collision. Give your name, address, and vehicle registration to other drivers involved, no matter what happened.

questions.question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?

options.text: It is safe to drive if you can walk in a straight line.
It is safe to drive if you are below the legal alcohol limit.
Alcohol affects your judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects your judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol damages your judgment. You need good judgment to react safely to road conditions. Any amount of alcohol can affect your driving ability.

questions.question: What does a red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Speed up to clear the intersection.
Continue through without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: Stop when the light is red. Stay stopped until the light turns green.

questions.question: At what speed can hydroplaning start?

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Most tires can move water away at speeds up to 35 mph. Above 35 mph, tires cannot move water away as well. Your tires may start to ride over the water like water skis and lose grip with the road.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right and slow down.
Drive to the right and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: Yield to emergency vehicles using sirens and flashing lights. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line mean?

options.text: Both directions can pass.
Only the vehicle next to the broken line can pass.
Only the vehicle next to the solid line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only the vehicle next to the broken line can pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate opposite traffic directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass. A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: There is a downgrade or hill ahead.
Road construction is ahead.
The road will narrow ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a downgrade or hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a dangerous downgrade or hill. The hill may be long, steep, or have sharp curves.
